To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the perturbative N2LO 3BF, with parameters chosen to reproduce the A=3 binding energies and Gamow-Teller matrix element, provides an excellent description of the nuclear matter equationof-state at densities up to twice the saturation density, with the saturation point being very close to the experimental one.

the equation of state of nucleonic matter is consistent with the results of microscopic calculations based on realistic interactions and the empirical saturation properties of nuclear matter are reproduced by our model.

the perturbative chrial interaction is capable of reproducing the nuclear matter equation-of-state at low densities, while at high densities the equation-of-state is too soft and the symmetry energy is overbound.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of nuclear matter with chiral interactions, which is an important ingredient for the understanding of the properties of dense matter in neutron stars.
a consistent perturbative calculation of the nuclear matter equation-of-state (EOS).
a systematic investigation of the properties of nuclear systems in the framework of chiral effective field theory (χ EFT).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the absence of any other experimental constraint, a consistent chiral N3 LO two-body interaction plus a N2 LO three-body force is able to reproduce all the low-energy two- and three-nucleon data and the binding energy of nuclear matter, at least in a range where the perturbative treatment is valid, i.e. for a density of 0.1 fm−3.
the N3LO two- body potential plus N2LO 3BF is a consistent and reliable approach to the nuclear many-body problem.
the N3LO two- body interaction plus the N2LO 3BF is able to reproduce the saturation properties and the equation of state of nuclear matter with high accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 3BF is essential for an accurate description of the saturation properties of nuclear matter and that the N3LO 2BF is able to reproduce the saturation properties with an accuracy of a few MeV.
the two-body potential alone leads to an overestimation of the binding energy per nucleon by about 10%, whereas the inclusion of the 3BF leads to an excellent agreement with the experimental data.
we have shown that the N3LO two-body potential is able to describe the nuclear matter equation-of-state in a consistent manner with the low-energy constants determined by two-body observabiles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a perturbative treatment of the 3BF, in the sense of a systematic expansion of the 3NF contribution in powers of the 2NF strength, is not justified.
a 3BF is needed to obtain a reasonable equation of state.
the inclusion of the 3BF is necessary to reproduce the saturation point of nuclear matter, as well as its compressibility.
